reason: Real but much narrower than stated. The global handler does emit str(exc) as a raw 502 detail (app.py:312-315) and unclassified ProviderErrors leak internals (the /quotes/ZZZQNOPE repro reproduces verbatim), and no failure message carries a 'what would unlock it'. But the claim that three panels print that string does not hold for this repro: /fundamentals already maps not_found/rate_limited to human 404/429 text (fundamentals.py:~103-114, live 404 'No instrument matches ... check the symbol.'); Watchlist uses batch /quotes, which silently drops a failed symbol (200, row gets a null quote, watchlist/api.ts:37-41); Chart's /history returns 200 with empty bars and reason 'in_eod_only'; Equity Overview uses allSettled and on all-failed shows 'No data available for X' (EquityOverviewPanel.tsx:754-756), so the catch at :763 is effectively unreachable. The leak remains only for unclassified (kind=None) errors: the single-symbol /quotes route, the fundamentals 502 fall-through (fundamentals.py:115 -> EmptyState hint at EquityOverviewPanel.tsx:1048), and the chart catch at ChartPanel.tsx:408. Secondary defect: a nonexistent symbol on /quotes/{symbol} is misclassified as an unclassified yfinance attribute error instead of not_found. Downgraded to low because common failures are already humanized and the remaining leak is a polish and edge case.

reason: Holds. On a native-search tier, the runtime sets opts web_search=True with web_search_max_uses=5 and strips the local web_search tool (agent_runtime.py:1335-1340). OpenAI/xAI/OpenRouter, Gemini and Groq adapters pop web_search_max_uses unused (openai.py:665-667, gemini.py:112, groq.py:117), and only Anthropic applies it, per request. The only loop counter (web_search_calls, agent_runtime.py:1416,1553-1556) increments on local 'web_search' tool calls, which are absent on that tier. This contradicts the native_search.py:109-113 docstring that promises a loop-level counter. No native-search usage is metered anywhere (grep for server_tool_use/web_search_requests/search_count finds nothing), and BudgetGuard prices tokens only (budget_guard.py:82-84), so per-search charges are invisible to the spend ceiling.
evidence_checked: Code-only (an LLM-backed repro would cost spend and is not needed). Opened the runtime, all adapter pop sites, the native_search helpers and budget_guard, and grepped for any native-search metering.
repro_check: grep -rn 'web_search_max_uses' sidecar/services/llm -> popped and discarded in openai/gemini/groq, used only in anthropic; grep for server_tool_use|web_search_requests|search_count in the runtime/adapters/budget_guard -> no matches.

reason: The spec/code mismatch is real: FR-003 (spec.md:829-831) still mandates four hotkeyed modes, while the code ships two, Agent on alt+1 and Delegate on alt+2 (agent-modes.ts:24,42-60; keybindings.ts:65-82). But the claim that there is 'no decision record' is wrong. REBUILD_SPEC.md, which calls itself 'a decision document' (:1-8), states at :179 'The spine is already **two modes** (agent/delegate, types/agent-modes.ts) — good', and REBUILD_R3_SPEC.md:235-242,299 schedules the four-mode to two-mode string cleanup. So the collapse is a ratified product call. What remains is drift: spec.md FR-003/US3 was never amended, and src/store/agent-mode.ts:1-8 still documents 'four-mode ... (⌥1–⌥4)'. Downgraded to low (docs drift, not a missing feature).
evidence_checked: Opened the modes type, the keybinding defaults and the agent-mode store; grepped DECISIONS.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/redesign and specs for the mode-collapse record.
repro_check: grep -rn 'alt+3\|alt+4' src -> no live bindings; grep -rni 'two modes' docs/redesign -> REBUILD_SPEC.md:179 endorses the two-mode spine.

reason: Real, and the mechanism is worse than stated. The raw finding says an operator/host-driven pause exists, but pause_run (run_manager.py:301-316) has NO caller anywhere. The runs router exposes launch/list/get/cancel/answer/resume but no /pause route (routers/runs.py:63-127), no agent tool calls it, and nothing in src references it. So a Delegate run cannot be paused for a question by anyone: the answer_run route is reachable only for a run that could never reach status 'paused', and run_manager.py:23-34's 'fully implemented' docstring overstates it. Severity stays low because FR-028 is a SHOULD (spec.md:883-884); the fix is an ask_user capability plus a pause route.
evidence_checked: Opened run_manager and the runs router; grepped sidecar/routers, sidecar/services and src for pause_run, /pause and ask_user.
repro_check: grep -rn 'pause_run\|/pause' sidecar/routers sidecar/services src -> only the definition and docstring in run_manager.py; no route, tool or frontend caller.

reason: The core claim holds: every first-party panel ships through a static import list (src/modules/index.ts:3-27,60-70 -> page.tsx:18,50 registerModules). That path skips the plugin runtime, manifests and the requiredHostVersion check. The spec clarification (spec.md:98-105) explicitly requires first-party panels to be pre-installed plugins that are 'not a separate hardcoded path'. The mechanism is overstated in one respect: the module registry is not a wholly parallel extension system. Plugin-contributed panels ARE adapted into it through moduleForPlugin (plugin-bootstrap.ts:127-160), so there is one host rendering registry and two registration paths. Users can also disable modules at runtime in Settings > Modules (SettingsPanel.tsx:1710+), though not install or remove them. Downgraded to medium: an architectural conformance gap with limited day-to-day user impact.
evidence_checked: Opened the module registry, the module index, page.tsx registration, plugin-bootstrap moduleForPlugin and the FR-050 clarification; listed plugins/ (no bundled plugin contributes panels).
repro_check: grep -rln panels plugins --include=*.ts -> only a broker adapter comment; src/modules/index.ts statically imports all core panel modules.
